title: The Garel maps assemble into a map of de Rham complexes compatible with the trace and with the Leibniz rule
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter derham.tex (de Rham Cohomology)

difficulty_reason: The proposition assembles the individual Garel maps into a map of complexes from the pushforward of the de Rham complex of the source to the de Rham complex of the target, compatible with the trace in degree zero and with the Leibniz rule, and descending to relative differentials over a base (statement lines 4187-4213, with a reference environment recording Garel's paper). The proof reduces the identities to the local model given by the universal finite syntomic families, uses that the model is smooth with the morphism etale over a dense open and that the target differentials are torsion free to pass to a split finite etale cover, where the checks are immediate, and then derives the relative statement from the Leibniz rule. The two-stage reduction is the substance, so the claim is H2.
